answer: An agent economy can anchor identity to a refundable stake bond: before an agent can trade, it locks funds that are slashed if it cheats. A single operator running many fake agents must fund a separate bond for each one, so a Sybil voyage across dozens of identities becomes expensive rather than free. Honest behavior over time earns the bond back plus reputation, while one fraud triggers a ripple of penalties: the bond is lost, linked accounts are flagged, and the attacker must pay again to re-enter. Cost scales with the size of the attack, not with a single account.
